title: Numerical very ampleness on a nodal curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Assume $X$ is smooth except at ordinary nodes with completed local $k$-algebras $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Cohomology means Zariski module-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], and $h^i(X,F)=\dim_k H^i(X,F)$. Let $A$ be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For every nonempty reduced union $B$ of irreducible components, suppose
$$\deg_k(A|_B)\geq 2p_a(B)+1,\qquad p_a(B)=1-\chi(B,\mathcal O_B),$$
where degree, Euler characteristic and restriction are [def-pc-degree-line-bundle, def-pc-euler-characteristic, def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $A$ is very ample in the complete-linear-system sense [def-sc-ample]: the evaluation map generates $A$ and defines a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(H^0(X,A)^\vee)$ pulling back the hyperplane line to $A$. Irreducible components have the meaning of [def-weil-irreducible-components].

source.place: Section 2, Proposition 2.5(iii), printed p.40; nodal specialization. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted primary text read online.

proof.text: By [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], applied to the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is projective in the sense of [def-kun-projective], $X$ is proper over $k$, hence of finite type. By [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent], $X$ is Noetherian. Fix any nonempty zero-dimensional closed subscheme $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $n=\dim_k\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)\leq2$. It is finite and affine by [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite]. Write $R=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ and $I_Z$ for its defining ideal.

source.place: Tag 0E3E, lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein; Tag 0E8X, lemma-tricanonical, length-two-subscheme method

proof.text: Suppose $H^1(X,I_Z\otimes A)\ne0$. Apply [lem-sfb-curve-ideal-h1-subcurve-obstruction]: its properness, reducedness, connectedness, dimension-one and invertibility hypotheses hold. It gives a nonempty reduced connected closed subcurve $B$ with $\deg_k(A|_B)\leq-2\chi(B,\mathcal O_B)+\dim_k\Gamma(Z\times_X B,\mathcal O)$. This $B$ is a reduced union of components of $X$: each dimension-one component is already an ambient component, and an additional zero-dimensional component would be an isolated point, contradicting connectedness and $\dim B=1$. For $T=Z\times_X B$, [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies $T$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$ for an ideal $J$ of $R$: the defining ideals of $Z$ and $B$ are added on affine charts. Thus $\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)\leq n\leq2$, including $T=\varnothing$. The asserted upper bound is at most $-2\chi(B,\mathcal O_B)+2=2p_a(B)$, contradicting the assumed lower bound $2p_a(B)+1$. Therefore $H^1(X,I_Z\otimes A)=0$ for every such $Z$.

source.place: Tag 0E3E, lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein; compare Tag 0E8X, lemma-tricanonical, final subcurve inequality

proof.text: The ideal sequence tensored with $A$ is $0\to I_Z\otimes A\to A\to j_*(A|_Z)\to0$: locally trivialize $A$ and it is just $0\to I_Z\to\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_Z\to0$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf, def-pc-module-pullback]. By [lem-sc-module-section-boundary-exact], every section of the quotient lifts, since its boundary belongs to the zero group of step 2. By the definition of direct image, $\Gamma(X,j_*(A|_Z))=\Gamma(Z,A|_Z)$. Thus the restriction $H^0(X,A)\to H^0(Z,A|_Z)$ is surjective for every nonempty $Z$ of degree at most two.

source.place: Tag 0E8X, lemma-tricanonical, passage from H^1 of the ideal twist to restriction surjectivity; cohomology.tex Tag 01DZ

proof.text: All closed points of $X$ have residue field $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. For $Z=\{x\}$, lift a nonzero fibre vector using step 3; this gives a section nonvanishing at every prescribed closed point. For distinct closed $x,y$, take the reduced disjoint union $Z=\{x,y\}$, of degree two, and lift the pair $(0,e_y)$, where $e_y\ne0$ in the fibre of $A$. This separates $x$ and $y$. Finally let $\theta$ be a nonzero tangent vector at $x$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. On an affine neighbourhood of $x$ it gives a $k$-algebra map $a\mapsto a(x)+d(a)\epsilon$ to $k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. Nonzero means $d(a)\ne0$ for some $a$; the image then contains $\epsilon$ as well as $k$, so the map is surjective. Its kernel defines a closed subscheme supported at $x$, glued with the unit ideal outside $x$, hence a closed immersion into $X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This is a degree-two $Z$. Trivialize $A$ near $x$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and use step 3 to lift $\epsilon$ times its frame on $Z$. The resulting section vanishes at $x$ and has nonzero derivative along $\theta$.

Apply [lem-sc-point-tangent-separation-closed-immersion] with $V=H^0(X,A)$. Properness was established in step 1; algebraic closedness and invertibility are assumed; step 4 proves all three section hypotheses, including generation at closed points. It follows that $V$ is finite-dimensional, evaluation generates $A$, and the complete linear system is a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(V^\vee)$ pulling back $\mathcal O(1)$ to $A$. This is exactly the required complete-linear-system very ampleness. No smoothness assumption on $X$ or Cartier assumption on the test subschemes was used.

source.place: Tag 0E8S, lemma-separate-points-tangent-vectors, with the explicit generation hypothesis of the cited DAG node

tool_uses.why: Projective (closed immersion into P^N, def-kun-projective) implies proper; the exact convention of the item, a generic scheme-geometric prerequisite, not a replacement for a unit step.
Noetherianity of a proper scheme over a field, used to identify one-dimensional subcurves with unions of components.
Zero-dimensional finite-type subschemes over a field are affine finite schemes, needed for the elementary intersection-length bound.
The ordinary module-cohomology section-lifting criterion applies to the ideal sequence; no étale or trace assertion is used.
Closed points over an algebraically closed field are rational, to form degree-one and degree-two test subschemes.
Generic proper-scheme embedding criterion after proving generation and separation. The unit has no replacement for this geometric tool.
